b: Abhilash Khandekar is a veteran journalist of a standing close to 40 years in Print & Electronic media. He wears many hats. Born in Mumbai, he began his professional career as a sports journalist with Free Press Journal…
f: Abhilash Khandekar is a veteran journalist of a standing close to 40 years in Print & Electronic media. He wears many hats. Born in Mumbai, he began his professional career as a sports journalist with Free Press Journal ( FPJ) in early eighties. He later shifted to political journalism to join the Hindustan Times as its head at Bhopal and then went on to become Editor of Dainik Bhaskar and its State Editorial Head in Madhya Pradesh and in Maharashtra. Widely traveled in India and abroad, Khandekar has authored two books on politics and history and a three on birds. He dabbles in environment in a big way and has been nominated by GoMP and GoI on several committees. He co-founded The Nature Volunteers (TNV) at Indore in 1992. Khandekar was elected unopposed the President of the Indore-based MP Cricket Association in 2019 and continued it upto Aug 2025. He had anchored a popular weekly environment programme on Lok Sabha TV in Hindi by the name Astitva. He is the Co-Director of the Bhopal Literature & Art Festival. Abhilash Khandekar lives in Bhopal and can be contacted at @Abhikhandekar1 and kabhilash59@gmail.com

CK Nayudu’s biography ⁠Fortune Turners - Story of India’s Spin Quartet. ⁠Guts Amidst Bloodbath - The Aunshuman Gaekwad Narrative. ⁠Fab Five: The Pandavas of India’s Batting Her Story, Her Glory: The making of women’s cricket in India Additionally, he has contributed chapters to several other books. By qualification, he is an engineer (from NIT Nagpur) and holds a MBA degree (from Great Lakes Institute of Management, Chennai). He currently works as a consultant in a multinational firm in Gurgaon.

b: Ajay Shankar is a former Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer (1973 batch) with extensive experience in public administration, energy, industry and economic policy. He served in several senior positions in the…
f: Ajay Shankar is a former Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer (1973 batch) with extensive experience in public administration, energy, industry and economic policy. He served in several senior positions in the Government of India, including Secretary, Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion, and senior roles in the Ministry of Power and Planning Commission. He played a significant role in the enactment of the Electricity Act, 2003, the launch of the National Solar Mission, rural electrification, and the development of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor. He also contributed to economic recovery measures following the 2008 global financial crisis and initiatives to promote manufacturing, investment and ease of doing business. He has served on the boards of several leading public and private sector organisations and is currently a Distinguished Fellow at TERI and President of the Foundation for MSME Clusters. He holds master's degrees in Political Science from Allahabad University and Economics from Georgetown University, USA.

b: Akshay Chavan is an author drawn to the currents that bind societies across time. Educated at the University of Lancaster, he spent more than a decade in the fast-moving world of digital media and e-commerce before…
f: Akshay Chavan is an author drawn to the currents that bind societies across time. Educated at the University of Lancaster, he spent more than a decade in the fast-moving world of digital media and e-commerce before turning back to the slower rhythms of history. Between 2017 and 2025, he founded and led Live History India, the country’s first digital platform devoted to history and culture, and wrote over two hundred articles exploring India’s social, economic, and cultural past. He now heads the Pratiti Foundation, which works with diverse communities to cultivate shared knowledge, skills, and enduring livelihoods.

b: Ambassador Anil Trigunayat (IFS Retd.) is a distinguished Indian diplomat with over three decades of experience in international relations, foreign policy, and economic diplomacy. He served as India’s Ambassador to…
f: Ambassador Anil Trigunayat (IFS Retd.) is a distinguished Indian diplomat with over three decades of experience in international relations, foreign policy, and economic diplomacy. He served as India’s Ambassador to Jordan and Libya and as High Commissioner to Malta before retiring from the Indian Foreign Service in May 2016. During his diplomatic career, he held important assignments in Côte d’Ivoire, Bangladesh, Mongolia, the United States, Russia, Sweden, and Nigeria. At the Ministry of External Affairs, he worked in the Economic, West Asia and North Africa, and Consular divisions, and served as Director General/Joint Secretary for Gulf and Haj affairs. He also served as Deputy Chief of Mission at the Embassy of India in Moscow. Ambassador Trigunayat is a Distinguished Fellow at the Vivekananda International Foundation and United Services Institution of India where he focuses on West Asia, Africa and Russia. He is also President of the Millennial India International Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture (MIICCIA). He also served on the Boards of NTPC and WAPCOS as an Independent Director. He holds a postgraduate degree in Physics and conducted research at Oxford University. Ge is a Rotarian and Peace Ambassador at Unity Earth Australia. He has authored - Evolving Security Dynamic in West Asia and India’s challenges and West Asian Dynamics and Indian Imperative. He also co-authored Red Lines Redrawn: Op-Sindoor India’s New Normal along with three senior military officers.

b: Anu is a lawyer, author, Founder Traditional Knowledge Council. She has vast experience in pharmaceutical and technology domain in India, China and US. Anu is a powerful voice bringing Indian knowledge systems into…
f: Anu is a lawyer, author, Founder Traditional Knowledge Council. She has vast experience in pharmaceutical and technology domain in India, China and US. Anu is a powerful voice bringing Indian knowledge systems into contemporary public discourse. Her latest book, Bishnois and the Blackbuck, explores how Dharma can save the environment, where sometimes laws may not be enough.

b: Anubhav Nath is a full-time arts professional with an interest in writing, social development, mentorship and historical automobiles. He founded Ojas Art, an arts initiative promoting Indian contemporary arts with a…
f: Anubhav Nath is a full-time arts professional with an interest in writing, social development, mentorship and historical automobiles. He founded Ojas Art, an arts initiative promoting Indian contemporary arts with a focus on the Indian Indigenous Arts. His initiatives include, the transformation of a heritage property into a bustling arts and culture center in Delhi. He curated the Indigenous Pavilion for the inaugural edition of the India Art Architecture and Design Biennale at Red Fort in 2023. Some other curatorial projects are: Freedom to March which travelled to Washington DC, London and Trinidad & Tobago; Expressions at Tihar a three-year project involving young prisoners and contemporary artists and Order in Chaos for the Lalit Kala Akademi. Nath established the Ojas Art Award to help recognise talented artists in the indigenous arts and is an advisor to art and literature festivals like Jaipur Literature Festival and Kabira Festival in Varanasi. He contributes to publications and has been a speaker at multiple platforms and is a member of the FICCI Arts & Culture Committee. He is a Trustee at Salaam Baalak Trust (SBT), an organization that provides education, vocational training and residential services to over 100,000 street and working children. He co-founded the Ramchander Nath Foundation, a not-for-profit organization that focuses on the dissemination of arts to marginalized communities.

b: Aparna Kumar is a 2002-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, currently serving as Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime & Headquarters, Lucknow. Over more than two decades in public…
f: Aparna Kumar is a 2002-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of the Uttar Pradesh cadre, currently serving as Joint Commissioner of Police, Crime & Headquarters, Lucknow. Over more than two decades in public service, she has held several important assignments, including Superintendent of Police, Deputy Inspector General and Inspector General, in Uttar Pradesh Police and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP). An accomplished mountaineer and adventurer, Aparna Kumar made history as the first civil servant and IPS officer to complete the Seven Summits, climbing the highest peak on each of the seven continents. In January 2019, she skied to the Geographic South Pole, becoming the first civil servant and IPS officer to achieve this feat. She also became the first Indian woman to summit Mount Manaslu in 2017. During her tenure with ITBP, she successfully led a special long-range patrol team that scaled six previously unclimbed peaks along the Indo-Tibetan border. A recipient of several prestigious honours, her awards include the Uttar Pradesh Rani Laxmibai Veerta Puraskar (2015), Yash Bharti Award (2016), Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award (2019), President's Police Medal for Meritorious Service (2020) and Utkrisht Seva Medal (2026). She holds a BA LLB (Hons) from the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, and an LLM from UC Berkeley School of Law (2024–25), with a specialisation in Law and Technology.

b: Archana Khare Ghose is a New Delhi-based journalist, writer, editor, art critic and curator with over two decades of experience in the media and publishing industry. Over the years, she has been associated with some of…
f: Archana Khare Ghose is a New Delhi-based journalist, writer, editor, art critic and curator with over two decades of experience in the media and publishing industry. Over the years, she has been associated with some of India's leading publications and media platforms, including The Times of India, Hindustan Times, India Today-Mail Today and Blouin Artinfo . Driven by an enduring curiosity and a passion for discovering compelling stories, Archana continues to bring the same enthusiasm and fresh perspective to her work. She is currently pursuing an independent career as an art critic and curator. Her curatorial debut was Bimal Das Gupta – An Ode to a Legend , presented by Dhoomimal Gallery and Gallery Silver Scapes at Travancore House, New Delhi, in November 2024. She is presently working on several projects spanning art exhibitions, books and other creative ventures, which will be announced upon completion.

b: Atima Mankotia has over 30 years of editorial experience in print, publishing and digital media. Recently, she worked as communication specialist at United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) and is now a Professor of…
f: Atima Mankotia has over 30 years of editorial experience in print, publishing and digital media. Recently, she worked as communication specialist at United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) and is now a Professor of Communication, Organizational Behavior and Human Resources at a Business School. She completed her graduation and master’s in history from St Stephen’s College, Delhi University followed by Post Graduation in Human Resources from XLRI, and then a Diploma in Journalism from London University. Currently Atima is pursuing her Ph D in – ‘Communication for Gender Based Employment Inequity in India’. She published her works of fiction Staring at the Square Moon in 2017 and Better than Sex in 2020, and her latest book All That She Left Behind all with a strong emphasis on women-centric issues.

b: Avinash Kaul is the author of The Next Mountain: Notes on Resilience, Leadership and Purpose (HarperCollins, 2026), written with Priya Kumar. Forced to leave Kashmir at seventeen, in January 1990, he studied in a…
f: Avinash Kaul is the author of The Next Mountain: Notes on Resilience, Leadership and Purpose (HarperCollins, 2026), written with Priya Kumar. Forced to leave Kashmir at seventeen, in January 1990, he studied in a makeshift school in tents, earned an engineering degree and an MBA, and spent 28 years in Indian media, 16 of them as a CEO. He was most recently CEO of Network18 (Broadcast & Publishing), and earlier CEO of Times Television Network. The Next Mountain reached No. 1 on Amazon.in in six categories at its launch in July 2026 and went into reprint in 10 days. He lives in Mumbai.

b: Bharati Chaturvedi is an environmentalist whose passion led her to establish the highly regarded non-profit, Chintan Environmental Research and Action Group. Her interests lie in the idea of circularity and leakage of…
f: Bharati Chaturvedi is an environmentalist whose passion led her to establish the highly regarded non-profit, Chintan Environmental Research and Action Group. Her interests lie in the idea of circularity and leakage of materials, power and access. She contributes a weekly column on environmental issues to the Hindustan Times and, as a passionate bird watcher, a fortnightly column for The Print, on birds. Through her many forms of working, Bharati platforms the extraordinary planet we inhabit, and the many innovative ways to mend what has torn. She occasionally writes on her other passion- contemporary art. Bharati hold a degree in Public Policy from SAIS, John’s Hopkins and a Master’s and Undergraduate degree in History from Delhi University. She lives in Delhi with her husband and two dogs. Her book – Namkeen Neighbour – is based on her stay in Pakistan.

b: Prof. Bhushan Patwardhan is a biomedical scientist, author and educationist. He served as Vice Chairman of UGC, Chairman of NAAC and Vice Chancellor of Symbiosis International University. At present he is Chancellor of…
f: Prof. Bhushan Patwardhan is a biomedical scientist, author and educationist. He served as Vice Chairman of UGC, Chairman of NAAC and Vice Chancellor of Symbiosis International University. At present he is Chancellor of Deccan College Post Graduate and Research Institute, National Research Professor (Ayush), Government of India, Distinguished Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University, IIT Kharagpur, and Western Sydney University Australia. He is a member of the WHO STAG on Traditional Medicine. He is among the world's top 2% biomedical scientists with 18,000+ citations. He has authored Integrative Approaches for Health (Elsevier, 2015), Innovative Approaches to Drug Discovery (Elsevier, 2017). His non fiction book Genome to Om (BluOne Ink, 2024) has received global acclaim. His Knowledge for Kids series, aligned with NEP 2020, comprises Ayurveda for Kids and Yoga for Kids (Sakal Media, 2025, 2026) and Gaumata: Cow for Kids and for Everyone (Ink OCCAM, 2026).

b: Chaitanya Prasad is a former Civil Servant, belongs to 1991 Batch of Indian Information Service. Currently Head of Communication and Outreach, Ministry of Education Govt. of India. His core areas of expertise include…
f: Chaitanya Prasad is a former Civil Servant, belongs to 1991 Batch of Indian Information Service. Currently Head of Communication and Outreach, Ministry of Education Govt. of India. His core areas of expertise include Communication Strategy, Geopolitics and Strategic Communication, Communication & Governance, Media Management, Public Policy and Governance, Foreign policy, Cinema, Softpower, Information policy, Dissemination and Outreach, Perception & Media Coverage and Analysis. He also served in the capacity of Head of the Education Working Group for the Education Vertical during the G20 Presidency of India. His responsibilities included strategy development, content creation, stakeholder collaboration and perception & communication outreach. He has rich experience in handling matters related to Cinema and News & Public Broadcasting. He served as ADG News, DD & Directorate of Film Festivals. He has led several delegations abroad at leading International Film Festivals and has extensively networked with stakeholders in the Media and Entertainment domain at the National and International level. He has published three books “The Age of Influence”, a compendium of articles on communication strategies, branding, soft power, geo strategic communication & AI and the role of communication in foreign policy practice. His second book “When Branding Met the Movies” was released at the World Book Fair, New Delhi by the National Book Trust (NBT). The book explores and narrates the journey of branding in cinema during the last few decades capturing the different methods, tools and ideas. His latest Book “What We Choose to See” was published in July, 2026 on Cinema, AI & Communication. Mr. Prasad also is a resource person on Govt. communication, Branding and Cinema at leading Training Institutes for civil service officers &. IIMs. He has a Masters and M. Phil degree in International Relations from Allahabad University and JNU. He has been a Commonwealth scholar.

b: Chetna Keer is a columnist, novelist, former journalist & guest faculty at IIMC-Delhi. creative writing mentor & poet. Her sixth book, historical novel "MAHARAJA'S MORAN - LOST QUEEN OF LAHORE" has gone global,…
f: Chetna Keer is a columnist, novelist, former journalist & guest faculty at IIMC-Delhi. creative writing mentor & poet. Her sixth book, historical novel "MAHARAJA'S MORAN - LOST QUEEN OF LAHORE" has gone global, showcasing at the recent Frankfurt Book Fair, after featuring on foreign RED FM TORONTO & SHER-E-PUNJAB VANCOUVER podcasts and at 'Global South' ANANKE LITFEST 2026. Chetna's fifth book, “Geisha in the Gota Patti”, was LONG-LISTED for the OXFORD BOOK COVER PRIZE 2026. She clocked over 25 years in journalism. Later, she was Creative Writing Mentor for Deepalaya's media program, in collaboration with McCandlish Phillips Journalism Institute, New York. Currently, she pens popular HT column “WITerati”. Chetna has authored six books. Her ‘Gulmohar’ Trilogy touches on contemporary concerns like climate change, war and peace. She was a Speaker at Whitmarsh Knight Memorial Lecture on Climate Crisis, 2019, BCS, Shimla. She has been invited to leading litfests, from Khushwant Singh Litfest Kasauli to Chandigarh's "Literati", Pune International Litfest to 'Global South' Ananke Litfest.

b: Chirayu Thakkar is the founding CEO of Centre for Strategic Affairs, a New Delhi-based geopolitics think tank. Previously, he was Assistant Private Secretary to the Vice President of India and a Visiting Fellow with the…
f: Chirayu Thakkar is the founding CEO of Centre for Strategic Affairs, a New Delhi-based geopolitics think tank. Previously, he was Assistant Private Secretary to the Vice President of India and a Visiting Fellow with the Stimson Center in Washington, D.C. He holds a Ph.D. in international relations, jointly awarded by the National University of Singapore and King’s College London. He is editor of two books, On China (with Amb. Vijay Gokhale) and India and the UN (with Harsh V. Pant). He comments regularly on international politics and security in print and electronic media.

b: Christopher C. Doyle has studied three Sanskrit texts of the Mahabharata since 2006. His research, which translates and explains the Mahabharata, is available at The Quest Club Gold on his website. He has written seven…
f: Christopher C. Doyle has studied three Sanskrit texts of the Mahabharata since 2006. His research, which translates and explains the Mahabharata, is available at The Quest Club Gold on his website. He has written seven bestselling novels: The Mahabharata Secret (2013); The Mahabharata Quest series, featuring The Alexander Secret (2014), The Secret of the Druids (2016) and The Khandavaprastha Conspiracy (2022); and The Pataala Prophecy series featuring Son of Bhrigu (2018), The Mists of Brahma (2019), and Sword of Fire (2025). He has also written two Audible Original audio shows: The Magadh Mystery ( 2022), and The Pandava Riddle, (2025). Christopher’s latest book, The Curse of the Kurus, the first book in the Mahabharata: The Itihasa series, released in September 2026.

b: Devanshi Khetarpal is a writer and translator. She is graduate of the Iowa Writers’ Workshop where she studied fiction as a Sonny Mehta and Truman Capote fellow. She is an MFA Candidate in Literary Translation at the…
f: Devanshi Khetarpal is a writer and translator. She is graduate of the Iowa Writers’ Workshop where she studied fiction as a Sonny Mehta and Truman Capote fellow. She is an MFA Candidate in Literary Translation at the University of Iowa and a Graduate Research Assistant for the University of Iowa’s International Writing Program. She received her Bachelor’s and Master’s in Comparative Literature from New York University, where she specialized in Italian Studies. Devanshi is an Associate Poetry Editor for The Bombay Literary Magazine and her work has been published in The Threepenny Review, The Masters Review, Indiana Review, Public Books, Scroll and Poetry at Sangam, among others. She is the recipient of the James Michener-Copernicus Society Award from the Iowa Writers’ Workshop, a finalist for American Short Fiction’s Halifax Ranch Prize, and the recipient of an Honorable Mention for the Prufer Poetry Prize. Her work has been supported by the Iowa Translation Workshop, Iowa Writers’ Workshop, Bread Loaf Translators’ Conference, Andrew Mellon Foundation and NYU Center for the Humanities. She translates from Hindi and Italian, and is currently working on a collection of short stories set in Bhopal and a novel. She is from Bhopal.

b: Devdutt Pattanaik is one of India's most respected mythologists and culture experts. For over 30 years, he has worked to make ancient stories, symbols and rituals relevant to modern times. Trained in medicine, he spent…
f: Devdutt Pattanaik is one of India's most respected mythologists and culture experts. For over 30 years, he has worked to make ancient stories, symbols and rituals relevant to modern times. Trained in medicine, he spent 15 years in the healthcare and pharmaceutical industry before turning full-time to the study of Indian and world mythology. He has written more than 70 books, including Business Sutra, Myth = Mithya: Decoding Hindu Mythology, Itihasa: History of Hindu Mythology, Book of Ram, Leader, Culture, Jaya: An Illustrated Retelling of the Ramayana, and Eden: A Retelling of Jewish, Christian and Islamic Lore. He has also written over 2,000 columns for newspapers such as Dainik Bhaskar, Indian Express, Tribune and Economic Times. He reached a wider audience through his TV show Devlok. Alongside his writing, he has brought his insights to business and media. He served for five years as Chief Belief Officer at the Future Group, five years as story consultant to Star TV, and five years as culture consultant to Mukesh Ambani at Reliance Jio.

f: Dinesh Singh has served as the 21st Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University. He has studied at St. Stephen’s College and the Imperial College. Jindal University and has held A Distinguished Senior Fellowship at the Imperial College and an AICTE Distinguished Chair Professorship. He is an Adjunct Professor at the University of Houston and the Chancellor, K. R. Mangalam University. He has authored several books, including 101 Twisted Tales. He has exhibited as a painter. He is fond of Hindi, English and Urdu literature and is an avid fan of Mahatma Gandhi. He is an acknowledged orator in English, Hindi and Urdu.

b: Dr. Ajay Kumar joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1985 and retired as Defence Secretary of India on 31.10.2022. He is B. Tech. in Electrical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, India.…
f: Dr. Ajay Kumar joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1985 and retired as Defence Secretary of India on 31.10.2022. He is B. Tech. in Electrical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, India. He is M.S. Applied Economics from the University of Minnesota, USA and Ph.D. in Business Administration from Carlson School of Management, University of Minnesota, USA. He held various senior level positions in the State Government of Kerala and the Central Government. From July, 2015 to November, 2017, he held the post of Director General, National Informatics Centre (NIC) and Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Communications and IT. He was appointed as the Secretary, Department of Defence Production in the Ministry of Defence in December, 2017 and later as Union Defence Secretary from August, 2019 to October, 2022. He has spearheaded several initiatives and reforms in his career in the Civil Service. These include corporatization of Ordnance Factories Board, Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDex), AGNIPATH Scheme (Agniveers), promotion of Defence exports in the Ministry of Defence. In the Ministry of Electronics and IT, he was instrumental in revival of electronics system and design industry through a slew of policy initiatives including Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme, Electronic Manufacturing Clusters Scheme, Preference to Domestically Manufactured Goods Scheme, Scheme for setting up semi-conductor fabs, Electronics Development Fund and Compulsory Registration Order mandating safety standards of electronic goods. As DG, NIC he was instrumental in launching various Digital India initiatives including MyGov, Jeevan Pramaan, biometric attendance system among others. While in Kerala, Dr. Ajay Kumar is credited to have revived Kerala State Electronics Development Corporation (KELTRON) during 2000-2002 period and scaling-up of IT investments in the State during his tenure as Secretary IT of the State. He has, to his credit, several publications in national and international journals including at ICIS, IEEE, IJEC, HICCS etc. He was awarded the "Silver Elephant" medallion by National Scouts and Guides by His Excellency the President of India, in 1994. In the same year, he also earned a citation by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India and was adjudged the "Outstanding Young Person" by the Junior Chamber of Kerala. He earned the Graduate School Fellowship by the University of Minnesota, USA for the years 2004 and 2005. He was adjudged as the "Electronics Leader of the Year" for the year 2012 for promotion of electronics industry in the country. He was awarded the Technovation Sarabhai Award by IESA in 2015 for his outstanding contribution to ESDM Industry and was also awarded the “Champion of Change” Award by CEAMA in 2017. He was also awarded Distinguished Alumnus Award (DAA)-2019 of IIT Kanpur. He was conferred Fellowship of the Indian National Academy of Engineering (INAE) for his outstanding contributions to engineering and dynamic leadership in engineering domain which have immensely contributed for the faster development of the country with effect from November 1, 2021. He has been appointed Chairman, Union Public Service Commission by the Hon’ble President of India on 15th May, 2025.

b: Dr. Rajiv Kumar is a distinguished Indian economist, public policy expert and author. He served as the Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog from 2017 to 2022, with the rank of Cabinet Minister. He is currently Chairman of the…
f: Dr. Rajiv Kumar is a distinguished Indian economist, public policy expert and author. He served as the Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog from 2017 to 2022, with the rank of Cabinet Minister. He is currently Chairman of the Pahle India Foundation, a public policy think tank he founded in 2013. His distinguished career spans academia, government, industry and international institutions, including the Asian Development Bank, FICCI, CII and ICRIER. He holds a PhD in Economics from Lucknow University and a D.Phil. from Oxford University. In 2023, he was awarded Japan's Order of the Rising Sun for his contribution to strengthening India-Japan economic relations.

b: Prof (Dr.) Ruby Gupta is an academic and award-winning author of 10 Books. She was the International Writer-in-Residence at the International Agatha Christie Festival in England, and the International Resident at the…
f: Prof (Dr.) Ruby Gupta is an academic and award-winning author of 10 Books. She was the International Writer-in-Residence at the International Agatha Christie Festival in England, and the International Resident at the Gullkistan Centre for Creativity in Iceland. Her espionage thriller, The Secret of Leifeng Pagoda, inspired by the true events of the mysterious deaths of Indian nuclear scientists and defence personnel, is being adapted to screen by Almighty Motion Picture. Her murder mystery novel, No Illusions in Xanadu is published by Bloomsbury, and, her suspense novel, A Degree in Death, was Long Listed for the Crossword Book Award. Her other books span literary fiction, non-fiction, and academic writing, and include: Love & Crime, Maya - A Novel, Khushwant Singh: Reality and Myth, The Fulfilment, Basic Technical Communication, Advanced Technical Communication and Creativity Decoded: Mind and Art of Selected Poets. Two of her short stories are published in an anthology by Penguin Random House & Romedy Now. She is a Double Gold Medallist in English Literature, an awardee of the GSE for USA by Rotary International, bestowed with the Pratibha Samman Award for Journalism, selected in the Top 50 Writers of India, and the recipient of the Nation Builder Award. Having worked as the Regional Correspondent for Mirror Today, Feature Writer for The Tribune and M.P. Chronicle, and Columnist for The Free Press Journal, she brings a journalist’s precision and investigative instinct to her storytelling. She has been teaching MBA/B.Tech/BA/BSc students, guiding PhD scholars, and writing for over three decades. Her books on Technical Communication, published by Cambridge University Press, are included in the syllabi of various universities. She was the Coordinator, DIT-MIT (USA) research programme, and Coordinator, World Bank Project under MHRD, Govt of India. An avid traveller and adventure lover, she has explored over 28 countries and is currently working as Professor & HOD at the ACC Wing, Indian Military Academy. Across her work, whether fiction or nonfiction, Prof Ruby Gupta weaves together research, mystery, human psychology, and real-world intrigue, establishing herself as a distinctive voice in Indian crime and espionage writing.

b: Dr. Shalini Chawla is a Distinguished Fellow at the Centre for Aerospace Power and Strategic Studies (CAPSS), New Delhi. She joined CAPSS in 2006 and has published more than 120 research articles in national and…
f: Dr. Shalini Chawla is a Distinguished Fellow at the Centre for Aerospace Power and Strategic Studies (CAPSS), New Delhi. She joined CAPSS in 2006 and has published more than 120 research articles in national and international journals on a wide range of issues related to Pakistan and Afghanistan. She has authored seven books and lectures regularly at various universities, think tanks, and leading institutions of the Indian Armed Forces and Foreign Service. She is actively engaged in India’s Track 1.5 initiatives. She received a Commendation and Badge by the Chief of Air Staff in October 2020 for her praiseworthy contribution to the Service. She is a visiting faculty with the Naval War College, Goa. She is a Faculty (PhD Supervisor) at the National Defence College, New Delhi. She is a Visiting Fellow at the Vivekananda International Foundation (VIF), New Delhi. She is the moderator of the study group, Pakistan Forum, coordinated by the VIF. She is an alumni of the Near East South Asia Centre based at the National Defense University in Washington, D.C

b: Dr. Usha Mujoo Munshi is a distinguished Fulbright Scholar, former President of the Information and Communication Society of India, and a pioneering professional in the field of information science and digital knowledge…
f: Dr. Usha Mujoo Munshi is a distinguished Fulbright Scholar, former President of the Information and Communication Society of India, and a pioneering professional in the field of information science and digital knowledge transformation. Associated with the India International Centre, she has received several international distinctions, including the rare Directeur d’Études Associé fellowship from the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l’Homme (FMSH), France—the first such recognition awarded worldwide in the field of Information Science and Technology. With over 165 research publications and notable academic contributions, including Data Science Landscape (Springer), Dr. Munshi has made significant contributions to scholarship, research and the evolving knowledge ecosystem. Alongside her academic and professional pursuits, she has cultivated a distinctive literary voice. Her poetry has appeared in publications of the Sahitya Akademi and literary journals, including the University of Pittsburgh's Setu. Her earlier collection, Verses Unveiled: Soul’s Odyssey, explored the inner landscapes of human experience. Her latest book, The Quiet That Remains, brings together retold narratives and original poetry, exploring memory, identity, human relationships, displacement and the silences that shape our lives. Her literary work reflects a contemplative engagement with the human condition, where personal memory intersects with collective experience.

b: Imteyaz Ali is an environmentalist and waste management expert with nearly 28 years of experience in solid waste management, plastic waste management, e-waste management, recycling, resource recovery and the circular…
f: Imteyaz Ali is an environmentalist and waste management expert with nearly 28 years of experience in solid waste management, plastic waste management, e-waste management, recycling, resource recovery and the circular economy. He is currently the Project Director of the Plastic Waste Management and Rag Pickers Upliftment Project at Sarthak Sanstha, Bhopal, an organisation he has been associated with since 1998. He has played a significant role in developing and implementing the Bhopal Model of Plastic Waste Management , focusing on sustainable waste management practices, resource recovery and the empowerment of waste workers. His work integrates environmental protection with livelihood generation, particularly through the upliftment of rag pickers and marginalised communities. He has trained over 86,000 people across India, including government officials, students, academicians, waste workers and community groups. He has authored 82 research papers published in national and international journals and professional publications, and has delivered lectures at conferences, workshops and academic platforms. He has served as a Governing Council Member of the International Institute of Waste Management (IIWM), Vigyan Bharati, and as a member of the General Body of the Disaster Resource Institute (DRI). Recognised with numerous national and international awards, Mr. Ali continues to champion sustainable waste management, environmental awareness and the transformation of waste into valuable resources.

b: Ishan Joshi is Director – Partnerships and Programs at Pahlé India Foundation, a public policy think tank founded by economist Dr. Rajiv Kumar. A media professional and policy analyst with over 30 years of experience,…
f: Ishan Joshi is Director – Partnerships and Programs at Pahlé India Foundation, a public policy think tank founded by economist Dr. Rajiv Kumar. A media professional and policy analyst with over 30 years of experience, he has held senior editorial and leadership positions at The Statesman , The Pioneer and the Singapore-based Asia News Network. He was also the Founder Editor-in-Chief and Director of Fomento Media, Goa. He has taught at Ateneo de Manila University in the Philippines and the Indian Institute of Mass Communication, New Delhi. His areas of interest include foreign policy, geostrategy, conflict management and international affairs. He is an alumnus of St. Stephen's College, Delhi University, and the University of Hull, UK.

b: J.S. Deepak is a retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer, Deepak has many decades of experience working for Government of India, especially in economic Ministries including as Secretary Telecom & IT, and…
f: J.S. Deepak is a retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer, Deepak has many decades of experience working for Government of India, especially in economic Ministries including as Secretary Telecom & IT, and Ambassador of India to the World Trade Organization (WTO) at Geneva. Deepak served as a Secretary and Joint Secretary, Telecom, Government of India, wherein he was responsible for the formulation of telecom policy and reforms in the sector. He spearheaded various initiatives for improving telecom regulation and led the team that designed and conducted the first spectrum auction in India in 2010. He was India’s Chief Negotiator at the WTO, for the RCEP agreement and the India-EU Free Trade Agreement and led trade negotiations in agriculture, manufactured products, services, rules, tariffs and subsidies and articulated the Indian position on e-commerce and investment. . Deepak is an MBA from the Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Ahmedabad and has been invited to lecture on subjects related to management, trade, telecom and communication at various leading institutions and international fora.

b: Jaspreet Bindra is the founder of AI&Beyond and Tech Whisperer Limited, UK. He was the Group Chief Digital Officer at Mahindra Group, a Regional Director at Microsoft India, and General Manager in the Tata Group, as a…
f: Jaspreet Bindra is the founder of AI&Beyond and Tech Whisperer Limited, UK. He was the Group Chief Digital Officer at Mahindra Group, a Regional Director at Microsoft India, and General Manager in the Tata Group, as a part of the select Tata Administrative Services. He was also a member of the Founding Team at Baazee.com, which later became EBAY India. He is a Senior Advisor for ThoughtWorks India, Inflexion Group and Ionic Wealth. He was an Advisor to PWC, Mahindra Group, and Findability Sciences. He was recognized as the inaugural ‘Digitalist of the Year’ by Mint and SAP, teaches at Ashoka University, is a Facilitator at Harvard Business and is the only Singularity University Expert in India. He is also an AI Coach. He is an MBA, a Chemical Engineer, and has a Masters in AI, Ethics and Society from the University of Cambridge.

b: Jerry Pinto is a well known poet, writer, editor and translator. He has an LLB from Government Law College, Mumbai and a degree in the humanities from Elphinstone College. He has written Em and the Big Hoom, a novel…
f: Jerry Pinto is a well known poet, writer, editor and translator. He has an LLB from Government Law College, Mumbai and a degree in the humanities from Elphinstone College. He has written Em and the Big Hoom, a novel that won him The Crossword Prize, the Hindu Lit for Life Award and the Sahitya Akademi Award. In 2016, he was awarded the Windham-Campbell Award for Fiction from Yale, USA. His next novel Murder in Mahim won the Valley of Words Award for Fiction. His third novel The Education of Yuri has been published to near universal acclaim. He has edited several anthologies including: Bombay Meri Jaan: Writings on Mumbai; Reflected in Water: Writings on Goa; The Greatest Show on Earth: Writing on Bollywood and with Shanta Gokhale, a collection of stories on Bombay-Mumbai, Maya Nagari. Mr Pinto is also a translator. He has translated Daya Pawar's path-breaking autobiography Baluta, Sachin Kundalkar's debut novel Cobalt Blue, Mallika Amar Sheikh's I Want To Destroy Myself, Ganesh Matkari's Half-Opened Windows, Baburao Bagul's When I Hid My Caste, Eknath Awad's Strike A Blow to Change the World, Vandana Mishra's I, The Salt Doll among others. With Neela Bhagwat, he has translated the women poet-saints of the Warkari tradition, collected in a book called The Ant Who Swallowed the Sun. Shanta Gokhale and Pinto have produced a set of parallel translations of the poet Sant Tukaram, Behold! The Word is God. He has also translated the poetry of Narayan Surve: In That Mill I Too Was Forged. His translation from Hindi of Swadesh Deepak's I Have Not Seen Mandu has been acclaimed. He has also translated some of Deepak's plays and edited and introduced A Bouquet of Dead Flowers: The Best of Swadesh Deepak's Short Stories and a book of Deepak's plays. His translation of Susham Bedi's Havan as The Fire Sacrifice has been appreciated. His first Konkani translation was Boy, Unloved by Dnyaanpeeth award winner Damodar Mauzo. His work in nonfiction is equally illustrious. He has won the National Award for the Best Writing in Cinema for his analysis of Helen, the Life and Times of a Bollywood H-Bomb. He has also written a biography of Chemould Art Gallery, Citizen Gallery: The Gandhys of Chemould and the Birth of Modern Art in Bombay. Most recently he has written a book on palliativr care in India: A Good Life. He has also written books for children. Anya and Her Baby Brother and My Daddy and the Well were on the Parag Honours List. Mr Pinto has two books of poetry, Asylum and I Want a Poem and Other Poems. Between 2002 and 2024, Mr Pinto sat on the board of MelJol which works in the sphere of child rights. He has judged The Sahitya Akademi's Award for Children's Writing, the JCB Award in 2025, the Mehlli Gobhai Award for Children's Book Illustrations, the Laadli Award for Gender Sensitive Writing, the Crossword Award for Fiction among others. He is the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the People's Free Reading Room and Library and the nominal male on the board of the women's archive, SPARROW. He has taught journalism at the postgraduate Social Communications Media course of the Sophia Polytechnic, Mumbai for more than thirty years.

b: Kishore Singh is a Delhi-based writer, columnist, art critic and curator, and a senior member of the leadership team at DAG (formerly Delhi Art Gallery), where he oversees exhibitions, publications and curatorial…
f: Kishore Singh is a Delhi-based writer, columnist, art critic and curator, and a senior member of the leadership team at DAG (formerly Delhi Art Gallery), where he oversees exhibitions, publications and curatorial initiatives. With a career spanning several decades, he has written extensively on Indian art and artists, and has authored books across subjects including art, history, travel and culture. His notable publication includes M.F. Husain: The Journey of a Legend . He has also curated several significant exhibitions exploring the evolution and diversity of modern Indian art.

b: In a career spanning over four decades in the Indian Army, General Shukla has seen extensive service in the field - he commanded, an Infantry Brigade in Counter Insurgency Operations, the Baramulla Division along the…
f: In a career spanning over four decades in the Indian Army, General Shukla has seen extensive service in the field - he commanded, an Infantry Brigade in Counter Insurgency Operations, the Baramulla Division along the Line of Control in the Kashmir Valley and a Pivot Corps along the Western Borders. An alumni of the Defence Services Staff College - Wellington, the College of Defence Management - Secunderabad and the National Defence College - New Delhi, the General Officer has served two tenures at the Military Operations Directorate dealing with Doctrines / Force Structuring and was the Director General, Perspective Planning, addressing issues relating to Military Futures and Force Modernisation. He has also been Commandant of the Indian Army’s prestigious training establishment and think tank - the Army War College. A professional aviator General Shukla has an abiding interest in strategic - military affairs. He has published more than 50 articles in journals and prominent dailies to include the Hindustan Times, the Indian Express, the Print, Economic Times and the Business World. He has also lectured / participated in more than 200 talks / seminars in India and abroad, to include the Chandigarh Military LITFEST (2020 and 2021) and the Jaipur LITFEST (2019). He is a Distinguished Fellow at the Centre of Land Warfare Studies (CLAWS) and has been elected to the Executive Council of the USI wef 01 Jan 2023. In recognition of his service of the most exceptional order, the officer was awarded the Param Vishisht Seva Medal on Republic Day, 2021. The Honourable President was pleased to appoint Lt Gen Raj Shukla to the Union Public Service Commission on 18 July 2022.

b: Dr. Madan Oberoi, a former Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of 1992 batch (AGMUT Cadre), transitioned to the private sector in 2025 as Director of Strategic Engagements and Chief Cyber Security Advisor for the APAC…
f: Dr. Madan Oberoi, a former Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of 1992 batch (AGMUT Cadre), transitioned to the private sector in 2025 as Director of Strategic Engagements and Chief Cyber Security Advisor for the APAC Region at Google Cloud, following more than 33 years of distinguished service in national and international law enforcement. He previously served as INTERPOL's Executive Director, leading technology and innovation globally. He holds a PhD in Cyber Security from IIT Delhi and completed post-doctoral research as a Fulbright Scholar at the University of Washington. Earlier in his career, Dr. Oberoi served as Advisor (ICT) to the Ministry of Home Affairs (Government of India), Founding Director General of I4C, Founding Director of INTERPOL's Cybercrime Directorate, and held several other senior positions within the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Delhi Police. He is also Distinguished Professor (Practice) in the Department of Information Technology at Delhi Technological University, and also at the National Forensics Science University (NFSU).

b: Major Gen Lakhwinder Singh is a third-generation army officer. He was commissioned into the Regiment of Artillery in December 1967. As a Captain he fought the India- Pakistan war of 1971 in on the Western Front. For his…
f: Major Gen Lakhwinder Singh is a third-generation army officer. He was commissioned into the Regiment of Artillery in December 1967. As a Captain he fought the India- Pakistan war of 1971 in on the Western Front. For his gallantry in the war, he was recommended for the award of Vir Chakra. As Commander of 8 Mountain Artillery Brigade during the Kargil War 1999, his innovative use of 155mm Bofors guns in direct firing role and plan of incorporating 100 such guns on the objective turned out to be a game changer. He earned the name ‘Enraged Bull of Dras’ for his technique of applying overwhelming firepower on the enemy. For his sterling contribution to our victory in Kargil, he was awarded the Yudh Seva Medal.

b: Malashri Lal, with twenty-six books, retired as Professor, English Department, University of Delhi. Publications include Tagore and the Feminine, and The Law of the Threshold. Co-edited and co-authored with Namita…
f: Malashri Lal, with twenty-six books, retired as Professor, English Department, University of Delhi. Publications include Tagore and the Feminine, and The Law of the Threshold. Co-edited and co-authored with Namita Gokhale is the ‘goddess trilogy’ on Sita, Radha, Lakshmi, and also Betrayed by Hope which received the Kalinga Fiction Award. Lal’s poetry collections are Mandalas of Time, shortlisted for the Tagore Literary Prize, and Signing in the Air. With Namita Gokhale she has published two books on Himalayan folklore recently. Malashri Lal has served as a member of international and national book award juries. Honours include the prestigious ‘Maharani Gayatri Devi Award for Women’s Excellence’ and the SETU award of Excellence. Currently, Lal is the Convener, English Advisory Board, Sahitya Akademi.

b: Meghna Pant is an award-winning bestselling author, screenwriter, journalist and speaker, recognised nationally and internationally for her contribution to literature, journalism and gender equality. She has authored…
f: Meghna Pant is an award-winning bestselling author, screenwriter, journalist and speaker, recognised nationally and internationally for her contribution to literature, journalism and gender equality. She has authored ten critically acclaimed books, including Boys Don’t Cry, The Terrible, Horrible, Very Bad Good News, Feminist Rani, The Trouble with Women, and One & A Half Wife. Several of her works are being adapted for the screen. Her literary achievements have earned her numerous honours and shortlists, including the Frank O’Connor International Award, Commonwealth Short Story Prize, Laadli Media Award, FICCI Young Achiever’s Award and The Shakti Award. Her short stories have appeared in international literary journals and anthologies, receiving critical acclaim. Pant has written over a hundred articles for leading Indian and international publications, including The Times of India, Hindustan Times, Vogue, India Today and The Huffington Post. A passionate feminist, she advocates gender equality and has spoken against domestic violence through TEDx talks. She has curated discussions on feminism and interviewed prominent leaders through digital platforms. Known for abridging the Mahabharata into 100 tweets, Pant is a sought-after speaker at major literary festivals and conferences. She also mentors young women through leadership initiatives and conducts motivational sessions for underprivileged girls.

b: Nayanjot Lahiri is Professor of History, Ashoka University and academic coordinator of the Centre for Interdisciplinary Archaeological Research there. She has authored and edited over a dozen books, including The…
f: Nayanjot Lahiri is Professor of History, Ashoka University and academic coordinator of the Centre for Interdisciplinary Archaeological Research there. She has authored and edited over a dozen books, including The Archaeology of Indian Trade Routes (1992), Finding Forgotten Cities- How the Indus Civilization was Discovered (2005), Monuments Matter – India’s Archaeological Heritage Since Independence (2017), Time Pieces – A Whistle-Stop Tour of Ancient India (2018) and Searching for Ashoka – Questing a Buddhist King from India to Thailand (2022). She won the Infosys Prize 2013 in the Humanities-Archaeology and was the 2016 awardee of the John F. Richards prize for her book Ashoka in Ancient India (2015). About the book (Bandhavgarh Beyond Tigers – Human Life in an Ancient Jungle, Westland Books). In every era, forests have been inhabited by humans, from prehistoric hunter- gatherers to traders and travellers. In this book Nayanjot Lahiri and her collaborators recount that history through the cultural imprints that lie scattered across the hill slopes, swamps and flatlands of the iconic Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve of Madhya Pradesh. Drawing on extensive field work, studies in archaeology, history and ecology, Bandhavgarh Beyond Tigers explores how human activity has shaped, and been shaped by the hills, forests, rivers and meadows of this remarkable landscape. Richly illustrated with more than 500 images, the book offers an unprecedented account of Bandhavgarh and addresses a larger question: how can archaeology be undertaken in India’s forests, and how can the evidence found there be woven into the histories that encompass not just rulers and kingdoms, but the landscapes and communities beyond them? A book of remarkable scope, this work is for anyone interested in the human histories hidden in India’s forests.

f: Nick Collins has spent his working life in maritime trade in senior positions in London, Tokyo, Singapore and Dubai. He combined this knowledge with his Cambridge History degree to write a three-volume history of global shipping. He identified the first sustained maritime network as India to Mesopotamia, probably also the longest lasting. The first volume, How Maritime Trade and the Indian Subcontinent Shaped the World: Ice Age to Mid-Eighth Century is published by Pen & Sword in the UK and by Garuda Prakashan in India. The second and third volumes carry the story through to 2025. He writes regularly at maritimetradehistory.com and nickcollins1953.substack.com .

f: Poonam Saxena is a journalist, writer and translator. She has had a distinguished career with The Hindustan Times, where she launched and edited the HT Sunday magazine, Brunch, for over ten years, before moving on to edit the weekend section. She has written extensively on popular culture, film, television, books and literature. She continues to do a regular column for Hindustan Times which looks at our past through the prism of Hindi literature and Hindi cinema. She translates from Hindi to English and her translations include Dharmvir Bharati's Gunahon ka Devta (Chander & Sudha, Penguin Viking), Rahi Masoom Raza's Scene : 75 (HarperCollins) and The Greatest Hindi Stories Ever Told (Aleph). She was also the co-author for filmmaker Karan Johar's memoir, An Unsuitable Boy (Penguin).

b: Ambassador Prashant Agrawal joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1998. In a distinguished career, he served in France and Mauritius; as Deputy Ambassador in Thailand; as Consul General in Hong Kong and Macau; as High…
f: Ambassador Prashant Agrawal joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1998. In a distinguished career, he served in France and Mauritius; as Deputy Ambassador in Thailand; as Consul General in Hong Kong and Macau; as High Commissioner to Namibia; and as Ambassador to Laos. He has held various roles in the Ministry of External Affairs, New Delhi, and currently serves as Additional Secretary (South), overseeing India’s relations with South East Asia. An IIT Kanpur graduate and member of the Aspen Global Leaders Network, he is a keen photographer, avid reader, connoisseur of Indian art and world heritage, and passionate about protecting our planet and fellow sentient travellers for future generations.

f: Prerna is an award-winning author and wildlife conservationist. She was formerly a member of India’s National Board for Wildlife and its Standing Committee. Her work focuses on the protection of wildlife habitats and the human-wildlife interface. She strives to mainstream nature and wildlife concerns across policy, media, and society. Prerna has authored The Vanishing: India’s Wildlife Crisis (Penguin Random House) and co-edited Wild Treasures , an anthology on Natural World Heritage Sites of Asia. A Chevening Fellow, she serves as a trustee of the Hathi-Sathi Foundation, which works to enable safe shared spaces for people and elephants in North Bengal. A PhD scholar from the University of Cambridge, she was awarded the Royal Geographical Society Research Grant as well Rufford’s Small Grant. She is a fellow of the Royal Geographical Society, and the Cambridge Philosophical Society.

He is the only Biopic filmmaker who has produced more than 50 biopics of great Indian Personalities like Gurudev Ravindranath Tagore, Kundan Lal Sehgal, S.D.Burman, Jagjit Singh, Bhupen Hazarika, Khushwant Singh, Ruskin Bond, Amrita Pritam, Sahir Ludhianvi, Meena Kumari, Majrooh Sultanpuri, Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, great lyricist Shailendra, Fanishvar Nath Renu, Neeraj, Mahakavi Pradeep, Rashtrakavi Maithilisharan Gupt, Vrindavan Lal Verma, Zohra Sehgal, R K Laxman, Major Dhyanchand, S.P.Singh and Rajendra Mathur. The names of a few books are: Hindustan ka Safar, Sadi ka sampadak -Rajendra Mathur, Krantidoot Pandit Parmanand, Shabd-Sitare.Mister Media, Kahan tum chale gaye- Dastan e Jagjit ( First Biography of Jagjit Singh) and Zindgi ka sath Nibhata Chala gaya (First Biography of Sahir Ludhianvi) He received many awards, like the International Mahatma Gandhi Award, Rajendra Mathur National Award, Adeeb International Award, National Suryadutta Award, National Jagjit Singh Sammaan, INBA Lifetime Achievement Award, Madhya Pradesh Ratan Award, Makhanlal Chaturvedi Samman, etc. He visited the United States of America for media studies and Nepal to cover the earthquake. b: Reela Hota, an acclaimed Odissi dancer, scholar, and yoga practitioner, seamlessly blends spirituality with artistry. An ‘A’ grade artist with the Central Sangeet Natak Akademi and Prasar Bharati, she has performed…
f: Reela Hota, an acclaimed Odissi dancer, scholar, and yoga practitioner, seamlessly blends spirituality with artistry. Under her leadership, her troupe has been recognized as ‘Outstanding’ by India’s Ministry of Culture. A distinguished scholar, she has presented papers such as The Spiritual Facets of Shringar Rasa and Transforming Anger through Odissi Dance. Awarded an Honorary Doctorate in 2022, she has received the Guru Gangadhar Pradhan Award (2024), Senior Fellowship from the Ministry of Culture (2019), Atal Bihari Vajpayee Award for Art and Culture (2018), and Sanatan Nritya Puraskar (2007). Her work bridges tradition and contemporary expression, inspiring artists and scholars alike.

f: Shashi Ranjan Kumar is an Indian civil servant, author and poet. He graduated in Electrical Engineering from IIT Delhi in 1989. A 1992-batch officer of the Indian Administrative Service from the Tripura cadre, he has held senior positions in the Government of India and currently serves as Secretary, Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). Alongside a distinguished career in public administration, he has pursued a sustained engagement with literature, science, history and the intellectual traditions of India. Kumar’s literary journey began with Samudra Tat Par (On the Seashore), a collection of poems in Hindi. The poems are marked by a quiet engagement with love, nature, beauty, memory and the passage of time. Kumar approaches poetry as a mode of recovering experience—of gathering fragments of memory, fleeting moments and the seemingly insignificant details of everyday existence. In 2019, Kumar published Mysteries of the Universe, a work that explores some of the most fundamental questions confronting human beings: Is the future predictable? How real is reality? What are the limits of human knowledge? Moving between science and philosophy, the book traces the human quest to understand the universe and, in doing so, offers a broad intellectual history of scientific thought. His most recent and ambitious work is The Decline of the Hindu Civilization: Lessons from the Past, published by Rupa Publications in December 2025.

b: Sudeep Sohni is a filmmaker, writer, and cultural practitioner based in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. He is the Founder-Director of Sudeep Sohni Films, an independent film production house, and Cinekari, an alternative…
f: Sudeep Sohni is a filmmaker, writer, and cultural practitioner based in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. He is the Founder-Director of Sudeep Sohni Films, an independent film production house, and Cinekari, an alternative platform dedicated to celebrating cinema and the arts. An alumnus of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, he is a distinctive voice in Central India’s independent cinema landscape. His multidisciplinary practice spans cinema, literature, and cultural exploration, engaging with themes of childhood, identity, cultural memory, and tradition through a sensitive, deeply personal artistic lens. His latest fiction short film, Jaggu Aur Magahari , recently received international recognition, with its European premiere at the Indisches Film Festival Stuttgart (Germany) and its Italian premiere at the Film Festival della Lessinia, Bosco Chiesanuova (Italy), alongside prestigious Indian film festivals. The film premiered in India at the Kolkata International Children's Film Festival in January 2026, organized by the Government of West Bengal. His acclaimed films include Tanishka (documentary feature, 2021) and Reminiscence of Gangaur (documentary short, 2023), both of which have traveled to film festivals across India, Germany, the USA, Bangladesh, and the Caribbean. Tanishka was nominated for the German Star of India at the Indian Film Festival Stuttgart (Germany) in 2022 . Reminiscence of Gangaur is recognized as the first film in the Nimari dialect to receive international screenings. Both the films were subsequently acquired for international distribution and released on Heritage – the OTT platform of The Archaeology Channel (USA). Thus, Sudeep became the first and only filmmaker from Madhya Pradesh to have films internationally distributed on the platform, establishing a notable milestone for independent filmmaking from the state and bringing regional storytelling to a global audience. His Hindi poetry collection Manthar Hoti Prarthana received the Vagishwari Puraskar in 2025 from Madhya Pradesh Hindi Sahitya Sammelan. His monograph Sahitya, Cinema aur Samay , explores the relationship between literature, cinema, and time. He also contributes regularly to newspapers and literary journals. A former pre-jury member of the Screenwriters Association Awards, he also conducts filmmaking workshops and lectures at academic institutions. Rooted in Bhopal, Sudeep remains committed to nurturing independent voices and creating meaningful, craft-driven cinema that inspires, questions, and endures.

f: Vijay Gokhale graduated from Delhi University in 1980. He joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1981. He was India’s Ambassador to Malaysia, Germany and China.
